## Define the cohort before downloading

Use study `skcm_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018`, mutation profile
`skcm_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018_mutations`, and sample list
`skcm_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018_sequenced`. The shipped sample-list metadata contains
**440 mutation-profiled samples**. Do not substitute the study's total sample count
when estimating a mutation frequency.

## Fetch the records

cBioPortal's [API documentation](https://www.cbioportal.org/api/swagger-ui/index.html)
explains the paths and projection options. The tested GET request is:

```text
https://www.cbioportal.org/api/molecular-profiles/skcm_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018_mutations/mutations?sampleListId=skcm_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018_sequenced&entrezGeneId=673&projection=DETAILED&pageSize=10000000
```

Repeat for **TP53, Entrez 7157**. BRAF is Entrez **673**; these are gene identifiers,
not UniProt accessions. This cohort/gene pair is small enough for one large page;
for a larger cohort use pagination and verify that all records were retrieved.

1. Use `jsonlite::fromJSON()` or `httr2` to read each result.
2. Retain gene symbol, sample ID, patient ID, protein change, protein start/end,
   mutation type and study ID. Set a clear gene column before combining the tables.
3. Cache the data and metadata. In snapshot mode read the supplied CSV and JSON.
4. Count records by gene and `protein_start`, excluding missing/unmapped positions
   only from the positional plot. Report how many were excluded.
5. Draw a two-panel lollipop plot with `geom_segment()` and `geom_point()`;
   `facet_wrap(~ gene, scales = "free_x")` permits different protein lengths.
   Label axes **Amino-acid position** and **Mutation records at position**.
6. Separately count unique mutated **samples**, unique **patients**, and exact **V600E**
   records. Use `protein_change == "V600E"`; a count of all position-600 records
   includes other substitutions and is a different quantity.

## Tasks

**T4.** What does the shipped snapshot show? `[ELO 9]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
There are **245 BRAF mutation records**, including **158 exact V600E records**, and **82 TP53 records**. BRAF has a prominent position-600 hotspot; TP53 changes are more dispersed. The selected mutation-profiled sample list has **440 samples**. These are cohort-specific counts from 2026-11-18; a future query can change.
:::

**T5. [VG]** A plot shows 245 BRAF records. Can you report 245 patients with BRAF mutations? `[ELO 9]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
No. One sample can carry several calls and one patient can contribute multiple samples. Count unique `sample_id` or `patient_id` for the intended unit, state the profiled denominator, and check assay coverage. Records with no mapped protein position still belong in relevant mutation totals.
:::

## Report checklist

State the cohort and selection, show the two-panel plot, quote calculated counts
with inline R, interpret the pattern, and explain at least two limitations. Name
all data sources and their retrieval dates and end with `sessionInfo()`. Then use
these skills in [your own report](capstone.qmd).
